# [CS044] Unsafe Memory Manipulation (unsafe-memory-manipulation)

reflect.SliceHeader, a uintptr kept across statements, or unsafe.Slice with an unchecked length.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-119](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/119.html) |
| **OWASP** | A06:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

The garbage collector does not treat a uintptr as a reference: a pointer stored as uintptr and converted back later may point to moved or freed memory. reflect.SliceHeader and StringHeader are deprecated for the same reason. unsafe.Slice with an unchecked length reads or writes past the allocation. Pointer arithmetic in one expression with unsafe.Add is fine.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
addr := uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(h))
return (*int64)(unsafe.Pointer(addr + 8))
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
return (*int64)(unsafe.Add(unsafe.Pointer(h), 8))
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [unsafe-memory-manipulation]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    unsafe-memory-manipulation: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore unsafe-memory-manipulation -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** unsafe-memory-manipulation
```
